identity.title: The debris disc of HD 131488: bringing together thermal emission and scattered light
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We show the first SPHERE/IRDIS and IFS data of the -rich debris disc around HD 131488.
The models suggest a gas surface density of $2\times10^{-5}~M_\oplus/$au$^2$ which is in agreement with estimates from ALMA observations.

question.value: Can scattered light (SPHERE) and thermal emission (SED) of the CO-rich debris disc HD 131488 be fitted self-consistently with a semi-dynamical N-body model, and what does this imply for gas drag, porosity and size distribution

evidence.quote: To further explore gas-dust interactions in an optically thin environment, in this paper we present the first spatially resolved scattered light images of the gaseous debris disc around HD 131488 obtained with the SPHERE instrument.
We use N-body simulations to model both the scattered light images and the SED of the disc in a self-consistent way.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01243.S.

claims.hypothesis: Can one dust model fit both scattered light and thermal emission of HD 131488
claims.experiment: Radiation-pressure-only MODERATO fits to SPHERE image and SED, then added gas drag by retaining sub-blowout grains
claims.result: Radiation pressure alone needs ~4.4 Mearth in scattered light versus 1.0 Mearth from the SED; with gas drag both are fitted with 1 Mearth and Sigma = (2.0+/-0.1)e-5 Mearth/au^2
claims.finding: Only with gas drag can scattered light and thermal emission be fitted consistently; the implied gas density agrees roughly with ALMA-based estimates

evidence.quote: Our study shows that only when gas drag is taken into account can we find a model that is consistent with scattered light as well as thermal emission data of the disc.
The models suggest a gas surface density of $2\times10^{-5}~M_\oplus/$au$^2$ which is in agreement with estimates from ALMA observations.

claims.hypothesis: Does DDA improve on Mie theory for modelling this disc's scattered light
claims.experiment: Mie plus EMT versus DDA with small vacuum voids, same fitting
claims.finding: DDA and Mie give similar results for spherical grains with small voids; Mie is adequate for this disc

evidence.quote: We find that when assuming grains of spherical shape and small void sizes, DDA and Mie lead to similar results for pure radiation pressure models.

claims.hypothesis: What is the porosity of the dust
claims.experiment: Phase-function comparison with HG g=0.67 and fit quality versus porosity
claims.result: Best fit P=0.6, lower values not excluded, P=0.8 excluded
claims.finding: Porosity about 0.2 to 0.6, consistent with a pebble pile scenario

evidence.quote: The scattering phase function indicates a dust porosity of $\sim0.2\ldots 0.6$ which is in agreement with a pebble pile scenario for planetesimal growth.

claims.hypothesis: Is the scattered-light radial profile consistent with the ALMA ring
claims.experiment: Compared HG, Mie and DDA radial profiles with the ALMA Gaussian ring
claims.result: Scattered light prefers little dust inside 88 au, unlike the ALMA Gaussian (width 46 au versus 30 au for an asymmetric profile)
claims.finding: The profiles deviate inside 88 au, possibly due to the low ALMA resolution; the outer regions agree

evidence.quote: However, the deviation of the profiles might be attributed to the low spatial resolution of the ALMA data.

claims.hypothesis: Does the disc show a blue scattered-light colour
claims.experiment: Reflectance at five wavelengths from IFS and IRDIS compared with models
claims.result: Weak decrease of reflectance with wavelength with large uncertainties
claims.finding: Slightly blue colour suggested but not constraining

evidence.quote: While the reflectance might indicate a slightly blue colour of the debris disc, the uncertainties of the observations are too large to draw any conclusions.

why_this_data.value: HD 131488 has an outstandingly high CO mass, making it ideal for studying gas-dust interaction

evidence.quote: The outstandingly high CO mass makes HD 131488 an ideal choice for a detailed study of the gas-dust interaction.

why_this_method.value: Semi-dynamical model gives self-consistent scattered light and thermal emission

evidence.quote: This approach guarantees that the models for thermal emission and scattered light are self-consistent.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Varying void size and orientation in DDA was not done because of the extra parameters and computing time

evidence.quote: We decided against a variation of the voids for our scattered light models of the debris disc around HD 131488 as this would open several dimensions in parameter space

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: High proper eccentricity (0.9) pure radiation-pressure model rejected: poor chi2 and too short a collisional timescale

evidence.loc: 5.5 Combining scattered light and SED models
evidence.quote: a proper eccentricity of 0.9 leads to a very short collisional timescale for the planetesimals.

limitations_admitted.value: Gas surface density is a rough estimate without uncertainties

evidence.loc: 4.5 Combining SED and scattered light results
evidence.quote: We note that this is a rough estimate without uncertainties as we do not have enough data on gas species present in the disc.

limitations_admitted.value: Disc extent beyond 90 au uncertain because of low SNR

evidence.quote: However, in this region the SNR is low so that the actual extent beyond 90 au remains uncertain.

limitations_admitted.value: Inner disc poorly constrained by the low-resolution, nearly edge-on ALMA data

evidence.quote: Due to the low spatial resolution of the ALMA data and the nearly edge-on orientation of the disc, the region within 88 au is not well constrained at long wavelengths.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas drag is implemented by setting beta to zero for grains with St<=1, a crude treatment, so the derived gas density depends on that assumption
Gas density and eccentricity are degenerate (e=0.5 also fits with half the gas)
Scattered-light SNR is only 3 to 4, so chi2 constraints are weak
ALMA role is limited to literature results and a 12CO position-velocity reanalysis with unspecified details
